definition: Infusion means the introduction of one thing into another, such as money, energy, or flavor.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word infusion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know infusion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Opening the windows sent an infusion of pine-cold air through the stuffy cabin.
A splash is much milder than an infusion — a token amount, a little color or a little cash, gone without changing anything.
A flood goes further than an infusion — an infusion spreads through the whole and improves it; a flood overwhelms the whole and replaces it.

An injection is quick, forceful, and local — the added thing lands in one spot at one moment. An infusion is slower and spreads: what is introduced steeps through the whole and changes its overall character. If the boost stays where it entered, injection; if it seeps everywhere, infusion.

A dose is a measured amount given deliberately, usually as medicine — its point is the exact quantity. An infusion cares about spread, not measurement: the introduced thing works through the whole it enters. A dose stays countable; an infusion becomes part of everything around it.

Then the city assigned it six art-school interns for a year, and the change crept in the way steam fills a kitchen.
